options: Using information from after the prediction time
Using a model with too many features
why: Correct: the model sees data that would not exist at the time of the forecast.
That is a long horizon, not a bias.
That is overfitting, a different problem.

questions.q: Which split is correct for a daily series?
options: First 80% of days train, last 20% test
Odd days train, even days test
why: Random rows put future days in training.
Correct: the test set comes after the training set.
Even days sit between odd days, so the model can interpolate.

questions.q: Select all the steps that must be fitted on the training set only.
options: The calendar (day of week) of a date
why: Yes. They are learned from data.
Yes. A fill value learned from all data leaks.
No. The calendar is a fixed fact, not learned from data.
Yes. Learned mappings must come from the training data.

questions.q: Train values: 10, 12, 14 (mean 12, sd about 1.63 using the population formula). Test value: 20. Standardize the test value with the training statistics. Round to 1 decimal.
questions.why: (20 - 12) / 1.63 = 4.9. The large number is fine: the test value is far above the training range.

questions.q: You forecast hourly electricity load for tomorrow. You add the feature 'tomorrow's actual temperature'. At 10:00 today you only have a weather forecast. What is the issue?
options: Leakage: use the forecast temperature that was available at prediction time
why: It helps in testing, but production does not have it.
Correct: train with the values you will really have, such as the forecast issued before the target time.
Temperature is numeric. The problem is when it is known.

questions.q: Your 7-day rolling mean feature for day t includes day t itself. The target is the value of day t. What is the fix?
options: Shift the feature by one step so it uses days t-7 to t-1
Remove the target from the table
why: A longer window still includes day t.
Correct: after a shift the feature only uses past days.
The target is needed. The feature must not contain it.

questions.q: A team reports MAE 0.5 with a random split and MAE 4.0 with a time split on the same model. Which number should they trust for planning?
why: Lower is not better when the test is unfair.
Correct: the time split matches how the model will be used.
Averaging a fair and an unfair score gives a number with no meaning.
